match.reason: No bank point teaches the range of goals a business typically aims for (profit, growth, market share, service, social and environmental goals) at Stage 5 depth; the closest matches cover goal-setting and decisions, vision and mission at Year 11, government trade-offs, or the definition of a business.

draft.title: The goals of a business
card: Profit
Profit is the money left after all costs are paid out of revenue. Most businesses aim to make a profit so they can pay owners and keep operating.
Growth
Growth means getting bigger, for example by selling more, hiring more staff or opening new shops.
Market share
Market share is the part of total sales in a market that one business wins from its competitors.
Other goals
Some businesses also aim for good customer service, or for social or environmental goals, such as hiring local people or cutting waste.
draft.remember: Profit is a common goal, but businesses may also aim for growth, market share, service and social or environmental goals.

a.q: Mia's café in Dubbo sells more coffee than the other cafés in town. Which goal is she mainly achieving?
a.why: Winning a bigger part of the town's coffee sales from competitors is market share. Profit would depend on costs as well as sales, and the case says nothing about costs.
a.clue: Think about her sales compared with the other cafés.

b.q: Tane's bakery in Hobart switches to compostable bags, even though they cost more. Which goal does this show?
b.why: Compostable bags aim to cut waste, which is an environmental goal. It is tempting to call it a profit goal, but the bags cost more, so it does not help profit.
b.clue: Look at what the bags do for the environment, not for costs.

problems.detail: The clue 'Look at what the bags do for the environment, not for costs' names the environment directly. It points straight to the option 'An environmental goal', so a student can answer without understanding the idea.

check.summary: Both questions and the card are correct. Question b's clue says 'environment' outright, which gives the answer away.
